objective: Attack nu_star-Q with unrestricted core reselection. Prove a support-independent objective-loss identity and a source-backed linear bound on the explicit dense-residual parameter region h<=r/20. The full two-level and both admitted stronger obligations stay open.

atomic_claims.text: Let M be the full-core fractional leaf optimum and rho=(C(r,2)+2M)/3-nu_star>=0. For any integral leaf allocation of mass U and compatible integer core packing leaving L core edges, the exact deficit is [2(M-U)+L]/3-rho. No old support is frozen.

Put h=min(min(p,max(a-1,0))+min(q,max(b-1,0)),max(b-1,0)). For r>=max(200,N_Dross(1/100)) and h<=r/20, nu_star-Q<=nu_star-J<=2(a+b)/3+r/6+5/3. An absolute all-order constant on this restricted class follows by a finite small-order bound.

An explicit Hamilton-cycle parity join and one residue cycle remove at most r/2+5 core edges, at most four at any vertex, yielding a triangle-divisible residual with minimum degree at least 91r/100 in the stated region.

Actual exact execution computes Q, not merely J, by core-packing enumeration and two rational residual LP implementations on all 149 capped boundary-inclusive tuples through r=4. The named r=5 case is extra, not a complete range. Twelve mutations are detected.

assumptions: Finite simple two-prefix split graphs, 0<=a<=b<=r, nonnegative integer p,q; exact edge capacities and tagged endpoint budgets.
C25 leaf rank charging is used only after reoptimizing on the full core with integer unit edge capacities, not on a fractional residual.
S1 is Dross arXiv:1503.08191v3 Theorem 7, printed page 3, with epsilon fixed as 1/100 and source order equal to r. It is source-backed, not a trusted attestation.
Q permits complete reselection of the integral core packing; changing an old support object is not counted as objective loss.
